ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: in the upper left of the figure there is an R–NH2 group, below the nitrogen there is a dashed-line/transition-state mark, and there is a curved arrow pointing to the carbon bearing F on the aromatic ring; the aromatic ring is a benzene ring, the top carbon is connected to F, the upper-right ortho position is connected to NO2, the bottom is connected to NO2, and there is also a curved arrow inside the ring. Reasoning: the problem requires ignoring arrows and transition-state indications, therefore the independent R–NH2 in the upper left is encoded as the fragment *N with a wildcard substituent connected to nitrogen. The aromatic ring part is a substituted benzene with two nitro groups and one fluorine; according to the specified method, start from a nitro-substituted aromatic carbon and write O=[N+]([O-])c1, traverse along the ring and place F and the other nitro group, obtaining O=[N+]([O-])c1ccc(F)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1. The two fragments do not form an ordinary covalent bond, so connect them using a dot.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First ignore all curved arrows and dashed/transition-state indicators as instructed. Encode the standalone R–NH2 group as `*N`. Then encode the substituted benzene: start at the nitro-substituted aromatic carbon as `O=[N+]([O-])c1`, traverse around the ring so that the fluorine substituent is at the appropriate adjacent/top position and the second nitro group is at the para/bottom position, giving `O=[N+]([O-])c1ccc(F)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1`. Join the disconnected amine and aryl fragment with a dot to obtain `*N.O=[N+]([O-])c1ccc(F)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1`.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct structure-to-SMILES transcription from the depicted connectivity; no alternative inference route is needed because the task is to encode the drawn species while ignoring reaction arrows.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the drawing as two disconnected fragments after ignoring the curved arrows and transition-state attack notation: a generic amine fragment R–NH2, represented with R as a wildcard atom attached to N, and an aromatic benzene ring bearing F at one carbon, NO2 ortho to F, and NO2 para to F. The ring is otherwise unsubstituted.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt instruction that the desired output is the SMILES expression of the shown transition-state structure and that arrows should be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use standard SMILES conventions: represent generic R as wildcard `*`, a disconnected fragment with `.`, aromatic benzene as `c1...c1`, and nitro groups in charged form as `[N+](=O)[O-]` or equivalently `O=[N+]([O-])`. Choose a valid traversal of the substituted aromatic ring matching the image connectivity.
